subject: Caching Issue with googleVis, RPostgreSQL, and Shiny

messages.author: d6ffe8b5633d6bb1
messages.subject: Caching Issue with googleVis, RPostgreSQL, and Shiny
parts:
Hello,

I have a Shiny dashboard of business metrics using plots from the googleVis package. The data that googleVis plots comes from a query stored in my server.R file; it is simply 

drv <- dbDriver("PostgreSQL")

con <- dbConnect(drv, dbname="", user="", password="", port="", host="")

rs <- dbSendQuery(con, "select * from mytable")
mydata <- fetch(rs, n=-1)
dbDisconnect(con)

When I start the Shiny server and open up the app for the first time, the query takes a brief moment to run and, upon finishing, Shiny displays the googleVis plots. If I decide to close the app and reopen it some other time, for some reason the app displays the plots instantaneously as if the query did not execute. Sure enough, the plots show the same old data as the first time the app was opened, implying that the query did not run. 

Is this a behavior of Shiny where it chooses to cache the results of the query and display it upon future openings (without running the query again) or is this more along the lines of some RPostgreSQL feature? When this dashboard was created months ago, Shiny did not exhibit this behavior; the query would always take a moment to run before Shiny displays the plots. This is a recent behavior, leading me to believe it has something to do with Shiny.

Thanks for your help!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Caching Issue with googleVis, RPostgreSQL, and Shiny
parts:
It depends on where you're calling this from. If it's outside the shinyServer call, it'll execute once and be available to all sessions. If it's inside the shinyServer call, then it'll execute for each session. See http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

If you don't believe that this explains the behavior you're seeing, please send a little more of your server.R. Thanks.
